name: Evans Scholarship
value: Full four-year tuition and housing at an Evans Scholars partner university; ongoing academic and program conditions apply.
deadline: 2026 application and school/club evaluations expected by September 30, 2026. Complete the 2027-28 CSS Profile and FAFSA by October 15, 2026; provide the FAFSA Submission Summary when available. Decisions finalized by April 1, 2027.
apply: Create an online account using a personal email. Submit a two-page, double-spaced personal/caddie essay, school and club evaluations, transcript, family financial statement, parents’ 2024 and 2025 tax-return front pages and current pay stubs. ACT/SAT scores are strongly encouraged but not required for the 2026 application cycle. Complete CSS Profile and FAFSA and apply directly to the partner universities assigned to your state.
eligibility: High school seniors or 2026 graduates/college freshmen with at least two years of regular successful caddying, continued caddying at their sponsoring club in the application year, above a B average in college-preparatory courses through junior year, demonstrated financial need, and strong character, integrity and leadership. University placement follows residence/caddying location; community living is part of the program.
notes: The dated August 2026 application guide confirms this fall’s dates and the 2027-28 financial-aid forms. The high school evaluation explicitly allows finalists without test scores. Full continuing-scholar academic and housing conditions are not stated in the public applicant guide.

name: Hagan Scholarship
value: Up to $7,500 per semester for eight consecutive undergraduate semesters ($60,000 maximum), calculated after other aid and half the FAFSA SAI. The brochure also lists $1,000 first-year college essentials through a personal brokerage account; international students are not required to open that account.
deadline: Fall application available September 1, 2026, due December 1, 2026. Spring application available January 15, 2027, due March 15, 2027.
apply: Create a username and password on the online application portal and apply once (applicants may apply one time only). Submit a high school transcript and a letter of recommendation. Finalists provide a FAFSA Summary (US citizens) or citizenship documentation.
eligibility: Class of 2027 at a U.S. high school, regardless of nationality/citizenship; at least 3.50 unweighted cumulative GPA and parents’ 2025 adjusted gross household income no more than $125,000. Must enroll at an eligible four-year college the first fall after high school and maintain a four-year graduation schedule. Community/junior colleges and online institutions are excluded. Apply for federal/state grants if eligible. Complete 240 paid, supervised non-family work hours January 1 through September 1, 2027 for the first fall disbursement. Homeschooled students are ineligible.
notes: Need-based merit award. Renewal requires 3.0 GPA each semester and 3.25 cumulative GPA after the first semester; disbursement requires 14 fall and 30 combined fall/spring GPA credits, while retaining the award requires 12 fall and 28 annual GPA credits. At least half the credits must be on-campus or hybrid. Annual 240-hour paid non-family work and mandatory workshops/submittals apply. First-year work shortfall prevents fall payment without forfeiting the whole award; later work shortfall forfeits it. Cannot combine with another last-dollar scholarship. Account balances managed for HSF are not cash awards. The dated 2027-28 brochure and current-cycle Q&A list $1,000 for first-year essentials; an undated overview still contains a conflicting $2,000 line.

name: Daniels Scholarship Program
value: Up to full cost of attendance through combined Daniels/partner-school funding; up to $25,000 per year at non-partner schools outside Colorado, New Mexico, Utah and Wyoming, or $7,500 per year inside that region. Four-year award with annual renewal.
deadline: Application period September 1 to October 15, 2026, closing at 4:00 p.m. MT.
apply: Register on the official scholarship portal. Semi-finalists provide essays, recommendation letters, qualifying scores, state-residency and citizenship/permanent-residency proof, the federal tax return listing them as a dependent, and FAFSA Submission Summary. Finalists interview; new scholars attend the June orientation conference.
eligibility: Graduating high school senior residing in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah or Wyoming; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; at least 3.0 unweighted GPA. ACT at least 18 in each category or SAT Math at least 490 and Reading/Writing at least 490. Household claiming the student must have 2025 adjusted gross income no more than $100,000, with $10,000 allowance for each additional dependent and review of other assets. Attend an accredited nonprofit U.S. institution; two-year college is allowed when pursuing a bachelor’s degree, but trade/certificate programs are excluded.
notes: The current Class of 2027 page prominently states September 1 to October 15 at 4 p.m. MT, although its timeline cards appear out of order. The portal returns a loading/CSS error during public review. Full renewal standards and current form questions are not publicly readable.

name: Ford Scholars Program
value: Renewable award of up to $40,000 per year. The amount depends on financial need, college cost of attendance and other scholarships received.
deadline: Complete the application and 2027-28 financial-aid Submission Summary by March 1, 2027 at 5 p.m. Pacific Time. Annual opening is December 1; the page does not explicitly date the opening year.
apply: Submit FAFSA, ORSAA or CADAA as applicable and upload the 2027-28 Submission Summary with SAI plus a PDF transcript (unofficial accepted). Complete college plans, activities, household information and personal statements. One Ford Family program application per student; finalist Zoom interview required. Recommendations and SAT/ACT scores are not required.
eligibility: Oregon or Siskiyou County, California resident for at least 12 months before college enrollment; public-college students must qualify for in-state tuition. Graduating high school senior/recent graduate or equivalent who has never enrolled full time in college, seeks a first bachelor’s degree, faces significant financial/social barriers, and has SAI no more than 8,000. Full-time on-campus fall enrollment at an eligible nonprofit institution based in the student’s home state; community college is allowed with a bachelor’s transfer plan. Eligible undocumented students may apply. Federally recognized Oregon tribal members may qualify regardless of residence, with program guidance. No minimum GPA.
notes: Specific program page and current FAQ confirm the SAI limit, in-state college restriction and full-time minimum 12 credits. Siskiyou residents may attend OIT, SOU or Klamath Community College if eligible for in-state tuition. No previously earned bachelor’s degree; online programs excluded. Current calendar/FAQ confirms March 1, 2027 despite an older March 2, 2026 date still near the top of the application page. Full renewal standards and updated personal-statement prompts are not public.

name: Academic All-State Award
value: $1,500 award to each of 100 Oklahoma public high school seniors per year.
deadline: Applications open October 7, 2026 and close December 1, 2026 at 5 p.m.; the official page does not state a time zone. All supporting materials must be received by the same deadline.
apply: Create a personal-email portal account and complete your own application, including an essay of no more than 500 words and PDF test-score evidence. Designate a school official to upload the transcript and verify eligibility. Request two non-family recommendation letters; one should be from a teacher who taught you at high school. Submit the application and ensure every supporting item arrives by the deadline.
eligibility: Currently enrolled Oklahoma public high school senior with ACT composite at least 30, SAT Evidence-Based Reading/Writing plus Math at least 1370, or National Merit Semifinalist status. Scores must come from a single national or district-contracted test date; superscores are not accepted. Selection includes academic achievement, leadership, community service, character and essay.
notes: One-time student honor/award for 100 public school seniors, with the May 8, 2027 celebration. September 2026 guide gives the 500-word essay cap and teacher-letter guidance but directs students to the upcoming portal for this year’s essay prompt.

provider: Idaho Governor's Cup (Idaho State Board of Education)
name: Idaho Governor's Cup Scholarship (Academic)
value: Academic award up to $5,000 per year, renewable for up to four years. This entry covers the academic track; career-technical awards are separate.
deadline: 2027-28 dates are not published in the pages reviewed. The state portal still labels its early-October opening as 2026-27.
apply: Complete the Idaho State Board of Education general scholarship application with a 500-word personal essay, documentation of volunteer work, community leadership and public service, and two letters of recommendation. Use a personal email address in Scholarship Idaho. For renewal, sponsor’s current form requires an annual full-time undergraduate intent declaration; that form is still 2026-27, so do not assume its January deadline for the next cycle.
eligibility: Idaho residents graduating from an Idaho high school or Idaho home school with an unweighted cumulative GPA of at least 3.5, attending full time at an eligible Idaho college or university, with a strong commitment to public service.
notes: Current state page supports the 3.5 unweighted GPA and required essay, service documentation and two letters. The renewal form is still for 2026-27 and has inconsistent January 30/31 references; it does not establish 2027-28 renewal dates or all continuation standards.

name: TILF Scholarships for UIL State Meet Competitors
value: Individual donor awards vary; the directory includes $500 one-year awards and awards totaling up to $20,000 across four years. Duration, payment schedule and renewal GPA vary by donor.
deadline: 2027 application available March 1 through May 21, 2027. All supporting items must be submitted by May 21, 2027; no time zone or clock time is stated.
apply: Complete the 2027 TILF common application, available March 1-May 21, 2027. Upload high-school transcript with SAT/ACT scores if taken (no scores if not tested), a recommendation from an eligible school administrator, parents’/guardian’s most recent IRS Form 1040 pages 1-2 or an explanatory letter, and the college aid letter or FAFSA Submission Summary with SAI. Red Oak and Moorad applicants provide additional statements. Donor-specific awards can require extra criteria.
eligibility: Graduating seniors with qualifying UIL academic state participation; specified essay/film finalists, second-day Cross-Examination Debate competitors, and top-10 teams per group in BEST/FIRST/RECF-VEX state robotics also qualify. Athletics/music alone do not qualify. Attend an accredited Texas college full time; general continuing college GPA is 2.5, with higher donor-specific thresholds. Some awards restrict college, major, home county, contest or citizenship. Funding is paid directly to the Texas college.
notes: Scholarship family with donor-specific terms. The 2026-27 FAQ reports more than $1.2 million across nearly 70 colleges as total program funding, not an individual award. Current 2027 application page confirms parents’/guardian’s most recent Form 1040 pages 1-2; redact Social Security and bank routing numbers. If unavailable, provide a parent/guardian explanatory letter. The directory includes a conflicting Roy award total/payment schedule and a Welch award closed to new recipients after 2024; consult donor terms.

name: Triple 'A' Award (Academics, Arts, Athletics)
value: A four-year $1,000 scholarship for statewide winners in Class A and Class AA.
deadline: The 2026-27 nomination form is available. Each school and administrative region sets its deadline; ask the school Activities Director and region secretary. No statewide submission date is published.
apply: Complete the typed 2026-27 nomination form, academic/arts/athletic essays, a final essay of no more than 300 words, and a school staff recommendation. Student and school official certify the form. Submit to your school; schools forward one senior boy and one senior girl to their administrative region by the local deadline.
eligibility: High school seniors with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher at nomination who participate in at least one League-sponsored athletic program and one arts or activity program.
notes: The current eight-page form was revised September 2026. The League describes a four-year $1,000 scholarship for four statewide winners, but the public documents do not explain whether $1,000 is annual or total or state continuation conditions. Regional dates must be obtained locally.

provider: Lilly Endowment Inc. (with Independent Colleges of Indiana and county community foundations)
name: Lilly Endowment Community Scholarship
value: Otherwise unreimbursed full tuition and required fees for four years, plus up to $900 per year for required books/equipment. Room, board and travel are excluded.
deadline: County community foundations set different deadlines. Tippecanoe County’s Class of 2027 deadline was September 8, 2026 at 8 a.m.; this is an example, not a statewide deadline. Ask your home county foundation for its date.
apply: Apply through the community foundation in your home county. The county foundation nominates finalists and Independent Colleges of Indiana makes the final selection.
eligibility: Indiana resident with a diploma from an accredited Indiana high school, pursuing full-time undergraduate bachelor’s study at an eligible Indiana four-year public or private nonprofit institution. The 2027 Tippecanoe notice requires graduation/diploma by June 30, 2027. Local county selection criteria, restrictions and procedures differ.
notes: 147 awards statewide; local county foundations nominate candidates for ICI final selection. Tippecanoe’s dated 2027 notice confirms its award coverage and expired deadline. County materials, eligibility details and ongoing award conditions must be checked locally; there is no uniform statewide essay requirement.

name: Mitchell Scholarship
value: $10,000 scholarship paid in four annual installments of $2,500. 200 awards statewide, at least one per Maine public high school.
deadline: Opens December 1, 2026. Due March 1, 2027 (college financial aid letter due April 1, 2027).
apply: Submit either Common App or the Mitchell application, not both. By March 1, 2027 provide the application, transcript showing first-semester senior grades, FAFSA Submission Summary and a recommendation. The top-choice college’s financial-aid letter is due April 1, 2027.
eligibility: Full-time Maine residents on track to graduate from a Maine public high school who plan to attend a two-year or four-year degree program at an accredited college. Selection is based on academics, community impact and financial need.
notes: Financial need, academics and community impact are selection factors. Current scholar rules require at least half-time spring enrollment, verified directly with the college; no minimum GPA, transcript submission or separate renewal application. Students have six years to receive four $2,500 checks and should report leave, transfers, study abroad or early graduation.

name: Stephen Phillips Memorial Scholarship
value: Published award range $500 to $20,000, based on unmet need; renewable for up to four undergraduate years with at least 2.5 college GPA and continuing financial need. Amounts can change annually.
deadline: For the 2027 application, high-school applicants may use the Early Response deadline of noon April 2, 2027; the regular deadline is noon May 3, 2027. Only one application per year.
apply: The 2027-28 online application opens in December. Enter household, academics, college choice and financial details. The current cycle guide requests a FAFSA Submission Summary, chosen-college financial-aid package and two essays. It requests both college and high-school transcripts for college applicants; high-school applicants have their counselor upload the transcript. High-school applicants use a school counselor as required recommender; college applicants use a professor, high-school teacher or community contact. Up to three additional recommenders are allowed, excluding relatives/personal friends. The FAQ describes exceptions for college students: the high-school transcript is optional after three college semesters, and continuing students may use their current-year aid package. Those exceptions and the FAQ non-filer form have not been confirmed for 2027-28. Submit once all required portal questions are complete.
eligibility: Permanent resident of Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island or Vermont; entering/returning full-time student (at least 12 credits) pursuing a first bachelor’s degree at an accredited U.S. institution. U.S. citizen, or noncitizen with lawful presence and employment authorization, or who files/is dependent on a parent filing a U.S. tax return. The criteria page says applicants should have 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale and skilled writing. Unmet need must be at least $7,000 and SAI normally no more than 13,000; special circumstances should be discussed with staff. Fund directors, employees, volunteers and their families are excluded.
notes: Financial need is required. The specific Award page publishes $500-$20,000, while the Who We Are overview gives $3,000-$17,000; confirm the individual award with the Fund. The dated 2027-28 guide confirms the core materials, but its college-student transcript and aid-package instructions differ from the FAQ exceptions; the non-filer form linked by the FAQ still names 2026-27. Those exceptions are not confirmed for this cycle. Criteria uses “should” for 3.0 GPA, so no hard 3.0 filter is claimed. Noon deadlines are published without a timezone.

name: Rodeo scholarships for high school seniors (Metropolitan, Area Go Texan, Achievement and others)
value: Posted high school awards: $5,000 per year, renewable up to $20,000 over four years for tuition/fees. The separate 2026 Achievement award for existing college Rodeo Scholars paid $4,000 per semester, up to $16,000 depending on remaining semesters. Next-cycle amounts and full continuation terms are not confirmed.
deadline: Class of 2027 dates not yet posted. The most recent posted cycle opened December 1, 2025 and the online application closed February 2, 2026.
apply: Use the online application and upload required documents, then ensure the school official completes its separate portion. One common application considers eligible senior award categories; only one Show scholarship may be received. Achievement is a separate application for existing college Rodeo Scholars, not a high school award. Current 2027 forms are unpublished.
eligibility: Posted senior guidelines generally require U.S. citizenship, Texas residence, graduation from an eligible school, FAFSA and a Texas nonprofit institution leading to a bachelor’s degree. 2026 Metropolitan required SAT 950 or ACT 19 and top-half rank; other categories have different rank, county or participation rules. Community-college entry may qualify with a bachelor’s completion plan. Existing last-dollar/full-ride aid was disqualifying under 2026 Metropolitan rules. Achievement is for eligible existing college Rodeo Scholars, not new seniors. Confirm 2027 restrictions.
notes: This family includes senior and existing-college programs despite the senior-oriented title. Current website says 2027 dates/information will be published in fall 2026. The 2026 senior deadlines were February 2 at 7:59 p.m. for applicants and February 6 at 4:59 p.m. for school officials; Achievement had June 25, 2026 at 4:59 p.m. Full future eligibility and award rules vary by program. Aggregate funds are program totals, not student award amounts.

name: Civics Essay Contest
value: The 2025-26 contest paid a $5,000 first-place cash prize and $2,500 each for second and third. The 2026-27 prize terms have not been posted.
deadline: The sponsor said the next contest would be announced in fall 2026, but no 2026-27 prompt, rules or deadline have been posted. The prior deadline was February 6, 2026.
apply: The posted 2025-26 rules required one original 750-1,000-word essay without outside help, a Works Cited page in MLA or APA format for quoted/paraphrased sources, and student entry plus student/parent release forms emailed by the deadline. Identifying details in the essay body/title were disqualifying. The 2026-27 prompt, forms and rules are not yet posted.
eligibility: Posted 2025-26 rules: New Hampshire students in grades 11-12 at public, private, parochial or charter schools in the state, plus equivalent-grade New Hampshire homeschool students. Future-cycle criteria are not yet confirmed.
notes: The 2025-26 topic asked whether AI companies should compensate authors, rather than requiring constitutional-case citations specifically. Its deadline was February 6, 2026 at 5 p.m.; 2026 winners are announced. No 2026-27 contest terms are published. Do not reuse last year’s prompt or release form for a new cycle.

provider: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion (OSAC)
name: OSAC Scholarship Application
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 600) through one application; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-28 applications open November 1, 2026. The general page lists an annual February 15 Early Bird drawing and March 1 final deadline, both 11:59 p.m. Pacific with next-business-day adjustment for holidays/weekends; it does not explicitly date those closing deadlines for 2027.
apply: Create or update an OSAC account, select eligible scholarship fund numbers and complete contact/background, college plans, transcript, activities chart and personal statements. Current guidance limits each statement to 1,900 characters including spaces; the fourth statement is optional. Donor essays/materials may be additional. File FAFSA or ORSAA for need-based funds. Follow transcript-upload rules and submit every material by the final deadline.
eligibility: Generally Oregon residents, with specific school/tribal/military residency routes, studying at Title IV-eligible U.S. institutions; military academies excluded. Seniors, GED/homeschool graduates, college and graduate students may qualify. Some funds allow eligible noncitizens or undocumented/DACA/TPS students using ORSAA; citizenship and residency requirements have donor exceptions. No grant refund owed or education-loan default under general rules. The current OSAC FAQ says temporary-purpose international students are not eligible for OSAC scholarships.
notes: More than 600 donor awards. Early Bird $1,000 awards are drawings. General continuing rules include satisfactory academic progress and usually full-time enrollment, with donor exceptions; individual value, duration and renewal depend on the award. The state explicitly confirms November 1, 2026 opening but no dated 2027 closing deadline was located. ORSAA instructions contain a mismatched aid-year reference for fall 2027. Select the application for the actual academic year of attendance; do not rely on that typo.

name: MaineCF scholarships
value: Individual award amounts, duration and renewal vary by donor fund; the foundation generally provides partial educational support.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund. Most statewide funds list May 1; some list March 15 or April 15. The page does not state the year, so confirm for 2027.
apply: Find eligible fund descriptions and follow each application route. The online system uses an eligibility quiz and common information with fund-specific questions; some awards use downloaded forms, school offices or institutional selection. Required transcripts, recommendations, financial information and essays vary. MaineCF waives FAFSA for students unable to file because of immigration/visa status.
eligibility: Most funds support Maine residents, with school, field, location, year-level or other donor restrictions. Some funds serve nonresidents studying in Maine. MaineCF encourages applicants regardless of citizenship/immigration status and weighs academic performance, need, extracurricular activities and work experience.
notes: Read each fund’s description. Current statewide listings show yearless May 1 and other deadlines; the FAQ says online submissions are due 11:59 p.m. on the fund deadline and paper materials must be postmarked, without stating a time zone. Specific 2027 terms are not confirmed. Renewable awards and institutional awards do not share one common set of rules. MaineCF requires awardees to return the Terms of Award letter by the stated date, typically September 1; most payments go directly to the college in early December for second-semester costs.

name: HCF Common Scholarship Application
value: Individual donor awards vary; no uniform amount or guaranteed annual renewal.
deadline: 2027-28 application opens December 1, 2026 and closes February 1, 2027 at 4 p.m. Hawai‘i Standard Time. Donor-required recommendations are due February 16, 2027 at 4 p.m. HST. Award acceptance is generally due June 1, 2027 unless the award instructions state otherwise.
apply: Complete the common application and upload a current transcript plus processed 2027-28 FAFSA Submission Summary with SAI if eligible to file. Complete two general short statements, each at most 300 words. Donor-specific essays, ancestry/affiliation evidence and recommendation letters may be needed; letters are not generally mandatory for submitting the common application. Recommenders receive private upload links. Accept any award through the Student Award Acceptance Form by its stated deadline.
eligibility: Donor criteria vary. Most funds require Hawai‘i residency, financial need and at least 2.0 GPA, with exceptions; full- or part-time enrollment may qualify. Award payments are limited to U.S. institutions and territories. No universal citizenship restriction or GPA filter is established by this family entry.
notes: More than 300 funds. The 2026-27 average $7,230 per recipient is historical, not a guaranteed student award. Annual reapplication is required; some funds offer renewals or renewal preference. The portal still displays the closed 2026-27 cycle; current dates and guidance come from the updated 2027-28 main page/FAQ. No universal recommendation requirement.

name: Statewide Student Aid Program
value: Donor awards vary. Current four-year program page lists $250-$7,500 per award; the general FAQ instead lists $250-$5,000, so a uniform range is not confirmed. Renewal is fund-specific.
deadline: For 2026-27, traditional four-year and graduate deadlines were April 10, 2026 at 5 p.m. Eastern. Listed adult/independent bachelor’s, associate and credential routes accept applications through December 11, 2026 at 5 p.m. Eastern. 2027-28 dates are not published.
apply: Use ScholarshipSource with personal email. Prepare essay responses, a recent transcript if enrolled within the last five years, FAFSA SAI documentation (ask staff for a non-filer alternative), and at least one recommendation received by the applicable deadline. Finalists may provide the college aid package and an additional form. Renewal/reapplication materials and conditions depend on the offer.
eligibility: Generally New Hampshire residents plus specified Vermont border communities and certain graduate medical students in Massachusetts/Connecticut. Students at accredited institutions, including out-of-state/international schools, may qualify. Four-year selection includes need, merit, community/work activities; some associate/credential programs do not emphasize academic excellence. Most funds do not restrict citizenship, but the FAQ says a small number do. Donor and program restrictions vary.
notes: Close to $8 million for nearly 2,000 students is aggregate annual funding. Main page and FAQ conflict on individual range and whether citizenship ever matters. Main age-based four-year routes and FAQ dependent/independent wording also need applicant-specific confirmation. Current portal is open for associate/adult bachelor’s routes only; full 2027-28 questions and dates remain unpublished.

name: Rhode Island Foundation scholarships
value: Individual fund amounts, duration and renewal vary. The current directory includes awards from $500 upward, with different annual or multi-year terms; no uniform award is guaranteed.
deadline: Fund deadlines vary. The March 30, 2026 announcement said April 13, 2026 was the first major deadline for most funds. This is not a confirmed 2027 date or a deadline for every fund.
apply: Browse fund criteria and follow the fund’s universal, stand-alone or nursing application pathway. Many funds share a universal application, while others use separate applications. The current directory labels listed applications closed; next-cycle full materials must be checked in the relevant pathway.
eligibility: Rhode Island students are broadly welcome, but each fund sets its residency, school level, major, background, need and other rules. Some awards serve seniors, college or graduate students or vocational study. There is no uniform GPA, citizenship or need requirement across the directory.
notes: The March 2026 announcement’s more than $4 million is total available funding, not a student award. Current directory examples confirm differing values, renewal and criteria, including funds without academic-excellence requirements. New-cycle dates/forms and individual award conditions are not confirmed.

name: VSAC-Assisted Scholarships (Unified Scholarship Application)
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 150); amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-28 Unified Scholarship Application opens October 1, 2026. Submit the USA and submit/postmark all required documents by February 10, 2027. The website says online materials must arrive by midnight but does not state a time zone.
apply: Use MyVSAC, select eligible fund IDs and submit one USA. All VSAC-assisted scholarships require a general essay of at least 250 words covering goals, financial need, service and uniqueness. Donor-specific recommendations, essays and transcripts vary. Need-based funds require FAFSA; Vermont residents’ processed FAFSA reaches VSAC automatically, while nonresidents provide their 2027-28 FAFSA summary. Label/upload documents as instructed or follow the mailed/postmark route.
eligibility: Usually Vermont residents and U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens, with donor exceptions. Programs may be at U.S. or Canadian colleges/training institutions. Fund-specific school, major, year-level, need, merit and service rules apply. Eligible noncitizen is broader than permanent-resident status; no universal citizenship filter is imposed.
notes: Current 2027-28 booklet pages 1-9 confirm dates and common materials. The booklet’s donor entries distinguish amounts, selection and renewal; full renewal instructions come in award letters. Outside scholarships listed separately in the booklet do not use the USA. Individual donor terms are not universal to this family.

name: NCCF Universal Scholarships Application
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: Most scholarships open December 15, 2026 and close March 2, 2027 at 5 p.m. Eastern. Separate funds may have other deadlines.
apply: Create a portal account, submit the universal base application, then submit each matching opportunity and its supplemental questions. High school transcripts are uploaded by the counselor; college students use an unofficial transcript. Recommendations, essays and FAFSA Student Aid Index or financial information depend on the fund.
eligibility: Funds serve high school seniors, undergraduates, graduate/professional students and adult re-entry students attending eligible nonprofit or public U.S. institutions, including trade and technical programs. North Carolina residency, GPA, need and other restrictions vary by fund.
notes: The page announces 2027 dates at the top but retains 2026 dates and instructions below. The FAQ states a minimum award of $1,000; coverage and continuation depend on the offer.

name: CFMT scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 160 funds); amounts vary.
deadline: General applications open annually December 1 at 8 a.m. Central and close February 1 at 11:30 p.m. Central; the page does not state the cycle year. Special funds use separate applications.
apply: Submit the general application through the CFMT portal. Special school and employer scholarships have separate application links. Selected recipients must complete follow-up forms by the stated June 1 deadline before payments to the college. For the general route, recommendations, transcripts and any supporting documents must also reach the online system by its deadline.
eligibility: Primarily Middle Tennessee students pursuing a college degree, with some funds reaching students elsewhere in the United States or internationally. School, employer, field, financial need and other restrictions vary by fund.
notes: Decisions are listed annually for April 15; follow-up forms June 1; college payments in mid-July split between fall and spring. These dates are not labeled for 2027. Individual amounts and renewal conditions vary.

name: ICF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 65 programs); amounts vary.
deadline: The main application season is January 1 to March 15, 2027. Listed funds also show different month/day deadlines or require contacting the school; confirm the year and full requirements for each fund.
apply: Select your Idaho region on the ICF students page and apply to each fund per its linked instructions (no single common application).
eligibility: Idaho-connected high school, undergraduate, graduate and nontraditional students pursuing college, trade, technical or certificate programs. Fund restrictions vary by region, school, age, employer, field, GPA and financial need.
notes: The directory includes institutional or school-administered awards and some funds not currently accepting applications. There is no single application or universal GPA threshold.

name: WYCF scholarships
value: Donor awards generally range from $350 to $8,000; individual amounts, duration and renewal vary.
deadline: Applications for 2027-28 open October 1, 2026. Guidelines list March 1 closing and July 31 acceptance annually without a cycle year; confirm the current fund deadline.
apply: Review the scholarship directory and apply through the WYCF portal. Upload a formal or official recent transcript showing cumulative GPA, financial-need information and Hathaway status as requested. FAFSA is recommended but not required by WYCF. Recipients submit acceptance and proof of upcoming enrollment.
eligibility: Mostly Wyoming county, school or statewide connections; graduating seniors, undergraduates, nontraditional students and some graduate or apprenticeship opportunities. Institution, field, GPA and other restrictions vary by fund.
notes: The annual July 31 acceptance deadline is required to avoid forfeiture. Renewal may require satisfactory cumulative GPA and enrollment evidence; fund-specific terms govern. Deferral needs prior approval and does not waive acceptance.

name: ArCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (dozens of funds); amounts vary.
deadline: Portal opens each year beginning February 1; deadline not posted.
apply: Create a scholarship portal account, complete the required eligibility quiz, then submit an application for each scholarship you want. Selected recipients provide proof of college enrollment; payments go directly to the college.
eligibility: Mostly Arkansas students pursuing two- or four-year college, vocational or technical training. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: The sponsor’s linked FAQ explains that donors set amounts and eligibility. Awards are paid to the college after proof of enrollment, rather than directly to students. Future fund-specific deadlines and renewal terms are not listed on the overview.

name: ACF post-secondary scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships (over 60); amounts vary.
deadline: Opens January 15 and closes March 15 (year not stated on the page).
apply: One login and one application in the ACF scholarship portal considers you for every scholarship you may be eligible for.
eligibility: Primarily Alaska students pursuing post-secondary education, including college, vocational and trade programs. Some funds also serve California students or younger students in special education programs. School, residency, field, GPA, financial need and other restrictions vary by fund.
notes: More than 60 opportunities use the common portal. Some donor descriptions identify renewal or reapplication options, but complete individual amounts, continuation and materials require checking the fund.

name: MCF scholarships
value: Donor awards generally range from $500 to $5,000; some are renewable, with fund-specific conditions.
deadline: The next scholarship cycle opens January 1, 2027. Individual 2027 fund deadlines have not been posted; directory entries still show 2026 deadlines.
apply: Create a portal account and use the optional eligibility quiz, or a fund’s access code. Submit a separate electronic application for every fund you want; paper applications are not accepted. Transcripts and recommendations follow the individual fund instructions.
eligibility: Montana-connected students; high school graduation, full-time status, school location, major, GPA, need and other restrictions vary by fund. Some funds permit attending outside Montana.
notes: Nearly $1 million was awarded across all funds for 2025-26, not to an individual. The linked FAQ is labeled 2026-27; it accepts official or unofficial transcripts and requires electronic recommendations when requested. Recipients complete an acceptance form, and college payments are normally split between fall and spring.

name: SDCF scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: Portal opens September 15 and closes March 15 (year not stated on the page).
apply: Register in GOapply using an email you will keep after high school. Complete the common application, review matched and statewide opportunities, then complete each fund’s application and uploads. The published guide requires clicking Submit All after completing the chosen applications.
eligibility: South Dakota students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: The sponsor’s three-page GOapply guide is labeled 2026-27 and describes approximately 360 opportunities. Matching does not guarantee eligibility; each fund must be reviewed. The portal requires signing in to see complete applications.

name: DCF scholarships
value: Individual donor scholarship amounts and duration vary; current 2027-28 amounts are not published.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted.
apply: Create a Foundant portal account and submit the appropriate general application. Some funds require supplemental information or separate applications. Complete every required section, document and recommendation by that fund’s deadline.
eligibility: Primarily Delaware-connected undergraduate and graduate students, with some funds including adjacent Maryland, New Jersey or Pennsylvania counties. School, field, GPA, financial need and other restrictions vary.
notes: The current linked compendium is for 2026-27: the general application deadline was March 15, 2026, with exceptions. It allows multiple awards without a stated cap. Its instructions require enrollment evidence before payments to schools. The $1,001,500 figure is total 2025-26 funding across 237 students.

name: GKCCF scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships (hundreds); amounts vary.
deadline: Portal reopens for the 2027/2028 award year in December.
apply: Create a portal account with an email you will retain, complete the general and college conditional applications, then submit additional information for each recommended opportunity. Prepare an unofficial high school transcript; the sponsor advises completing FAFSA before the general application.
eligibility: Students in and around Kansas City. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: The sponsor says 2027-28 applications reopen in December, without an exact date or closing schedule. Each opportunity sets its own deadline and allowable costs; payments most often go to the college for tuition, fees or books.

name: CFSEM scholarship application
value: Most donor awards range from $250 to $7,500; most are one-time, with some renewable or allowing reapplication.
deadline: 2027 cycle not yet open. The 2026 cycle ran January 26 to March 16, 2026.
apply: One common application covers directly managed funds. The published 2026 instructions required a transcript, two recommendations, activities and employment information, essays and financial information including FAFSA confirmation showing estimated Student Aid Index. School-based awards have separate forms; confirm 2027 requirements.
eligibility: Students in Southeast Michigan. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: The sponsor explicitly says the displayed instructions are for the closed 2026 cycle and will be updated for 2027. The FAQ accepts official or unofficial transcripts with GPA on a 4.0 unweighted scale; renewal/reapplication depends on the fund. Payments go to the institution after a School of Choice form.

name: CFM scholarships platform
value: Individual amounts and duration vary by scholarship; 2027 award terms are not yet published.
deadline: The 2027 cycle is not posted. In 2026, applications opened January 15 and most closed April 15 at 11:59 p.m.; some funds had earlier or separate deadlines.
apply: Use the common portal application for participating funds and complete each fund’s supporting documents. Some awards instead require a school, university department or outside administrator; check the specific listing.
eligibility: Primarily Mississippi-connected graduating seniors, with undergraduate junior/senior, graduate and other opportunities. Citizenship, residence, school, field, GPA, need and nomination rules vary by fund.
notes: More than $170,000 is aggregate scholarship funding, not an individual award. The current directory includes one-year/nonrenewable awards, funds permitting reapplication, institution-administered awards and guidelines still marked coming soon.

name: CFT universal scholarship application
value: Donor scholarship amounts, duration and renewal vary by fund.
deadline: Universal application reopens in January 2027. 2026 fund deadlines ranged from February 13 to May 15.
apply: Use the CFT universal portal application and complete each fund’s required financial section, essays, recommendations, transcript or other documents. Requirements differ; no documents are accepted outside the portal or after the fund deadline.
eligibility: Primarily North Texas students, with some statewide, national and other-state school or employer funds. High school, undergraduate, graduate and vocational opportunities have different residence, citizenship, GPA, testing, need and enrollment rules.
notes: The application page confirms reopening in January 2027 but still lists 2026 donor deadlines. Published donor examples have different award and continuation rules; one C.V.M. entry conflicts between $10,000 and $15,000. Aggregate foundation funding and recipient counts are not individual award values.

name: ACF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund. The page lists the 2026-27 school year application; confirm 2027-28 dates.
apply: Complete the eligibility questionnaire in the student portal, then the matched application and required uploads. Prepare a recent transcript and applicable FAFSA financial summary, essays or online recommendations. The portal matches funds automatically rather than letting students select them individually; some institutional awards use another portal.
eligibility: Primarily New Mexico residents pursuing eligible nonprofit accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate study. Most funds consider financial need, full-time enrollment and GPA, but exceptions and specific school, field or other restrictions vary.
notes: The overview still advertises 2026-27 applications. The deadline page lists January 30, April 2 and June 4, 2026 at 5 p.m. in the sponsor’s stated MST zone, plus a separate CNM route. Renewal is not automatic: generally reapply annually, with some committed awards requiring a follow-up form. Scholarships provide partial support and are paid to the school after acceptance.

provider: Washington Scholarship Coalition and Washington Student Achievement Council
name: theWashBoard.org
value: Many scholarships from Washington providers; free matching service; amounts vary.
deadline: Varies by scholarship.
apply: Create a free profile, verify your email and review scholarship matches. Submit a separate application for each selected scholarship and its required materials. Updating the profile later does not automatically update applications already created.
eligibility: Washington residents and students attending college in Washington, including students who attended high school elsewhere. The directory includes opportunities from middle school through graduate school; each provider sets its own requirements and preferences.
notes: WSAC identifies the site as its program. The help page explains that old listings remain until providers renew them; use the active-scholarship filter and verify the individual cycle. Matching and preferred criteria do not guarantee an award.

name: CFNN scholarship portal
value: The FAQ describes individual awards of $1,000 to $5,000 for a single year; some funds have renewable multi-year awards with their own conditions.
deadline: Most listed general-fund deadlines are from 2026. The separate Lymbery certification page says it is open year-round with rolling review, but the directory shows January 1, 2027 for that same opportunity. The 2027–28 general season is not posted.
apply: Complete the eligibility quiz and apply through the portal to matching funds. The FAQ lists transcripts, FAFSA Submission Summary and SAT/ACT only where applicable. Fund-specific essays, recommendations and additional materials may be required; submitted applications cannot be edited without staff assistance.
eligibility: Mostly Northern Nevada students, including graduating seniors, college and graduate students, trade/certificate candidates and adult learners. Some funds include Hawaii or other locations, with county, school, employer, field, need and achievement requirements varying.
notes: The specific Lymbery certification page states year-round rolling review and requires an essay and employer/mentor or school recommendation. It differs from the directory’s January 1, 2027 date. Renewal may be one-year or multi-year depending on donor terms. Lymbery certification also requires acceptance from the chosen institution, trade school or certification program, in addition to its essay and employer/mentor or school recommendation.

name: OCCF scholarships
value: Donor awards generally range from $2,000 to $20,000; amounts may change annually and duration and renewal vary.
deadline: Fall 2027–Spring 2028 applications open October 1, 2026. Fund deadlines begin December 2, 2026; the major universal deadline is February 15, 2027. Check the matching opportunity for its exact deadline and time.
apply: Complete the free OCCF universal application in the scholarship portal and review each matching fund’s requirements. Request recommendations through the portal where required. Selected recipients complete a follow-up form and have the college registrar return verification of enrollment before payment.
eligibility: Primarily Oklahoma-connected students, including graduating seniors, college or trade students, adult learners and students with disabilities. School, region, ancestry, field, GPA, need and nomination requirements vary by fund.
notes: The main page posts new 2027-28 dates; the FAQ still gives December 3, 2025 for some older early-deadline programs. Use the current opportunity’s deadline. Award letters govern individual terms, and payments go directly to the college.

name: CFO scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (over 100); amounts vary (for example, Tulsa Engineering Scholarship $24,000 at $3,000 per semester).
deadline: The opportunity list does not publish 2027 application deadlines. Semester updates for existing multi-semester awards are listed annually for January 20 and June 15, without a cycle year.
apply: Use the CFO scholarship portal and review the matching application requirements. Existing multi-semester recipients generally submit a semester update after each term; CFO verifies enrollment with the school before payment.
eligibility: Primarily Oklahoma residents or graduates of specified schools, with some opportunities also including Kansas counties or alumni descendants elsewhere. Graduating seniors, college and graduate students and nontraditional learners have different GPA, field, need and other restrictions.
notes: The directory confirms Tulsa Engineering’s $24,000 total at $3,000 per semester, but full continuation standards are in the Student Agreement. Most multi-semester awards require updates January 20 and June 15. Payments go to the institution; notify CFO of transfers.

name: Pittsburgh Foundation scholarships
value: Individual donor award amounts, duration and renewal vary by fund.
deadline: Applications reopen for the 2027-28 academic year in January 2027.
apply: Search the foundation’s scholarships, then follow the listed route. Foundation-managed funds require separate applications, with a Copy Previous Answers option. Scholarship America programs may use a common application; institution-specific funds require contacting the school or following its instructions.
eligibility: Primarily Pittsburgh and Westmoreland-connected students, with high school, undergraduate, graduate/professional, vocational, adult re-entry and some K–12/enrichment opportunities. The general college guide states a 2.0 minimum GPA, but specific funds have their own school, residency, GPA, field and need restrictions.
notes: Nearly $3 million is total annual funding across approximately 375 funds, not an individual award. The main page confirms January 2027 reopening for 2027-28; exact fund deadlines and new application questions are not posted. References are typically two, sometimes three, depending on the fund.

name: CFWM scholarship application
value: Up to $3,000 total in scholarships per student per award year. Awards cover one academic year; reapplication is required and future awards are not guaranteed.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-27 application ran January 1 to March 1, 2026.
apply: Submit one scholarship application with a recent official or unofficial transcript, applicable next-year FAFSA Submission Summary, MASFA or Hartford County AACTUS documentation, and at least one essay. Students ineligible for the listed aid forms should contact the Education Team. The foundation matches funds automatically; loans require a separate application.
eligibility: Primarily Franklin, Hampshire and Hampden County residents, with some funds for Berkshire County, Hartford County, Connecticut or other areas. Eligible students generally attend accredited U.S. post-secondary institutions full or part time as undergraduates or graduate students; specific fund restrictions vary.
notes: About $1.4 million is aggregate annual scholarship funding. Awards are for one year and paid to the college after an acceptance form. Aid documentation must be for the upcoming academic year; the FAQ requests the full FAFSA summary, not only its confirmation page. Scholarship expenses are restricted to tuition and fees below six credits and tuition at for-profit institutions. The posted 2026-27 deadline was March 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m., with no stated time zone.

name: FFTC scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 150 funds); amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-2028 application cycle opens December 1, 2026 and runs to March 5, 2027.
apply: Search the FFTC portal and create an account. Complete each fund’s application, prequalification questions and required uploads; most request a transcript, references, financial-aid information, resume or essays. FAFSA-ineligible applicants may submit an explanation. Online submission is required unless the fund states otherwise.
eligibility: Primarily Carolinas-connected students, including high school seniors, college and graduate students and nontraditional learners; the broader fund directory also includes pre-K and school programs. Residency, school, field, need, GPA and other restrictions vary by fund.
notes: The main page explicitly posts December 1, 2026–March 5, 2027 for 2027-28. No common closing time or time zone is stated. The FAQ retains older SAR/EFC financial terminology, so confirm current documentation in the application. Recipients submit an acceptance form, and payments go to the institution; notify FFTC of status changes.

name: BGCF scholarship portal
value: Individual awards range from a one-time $1,000 to renewable $10,000 per year for up to four undergraduate years; amounts and continuation requirements vary by fund.
deadline: The 2027 cycle is not posted. The 2026-27 portal opened December 15, 2025 and its deadline was extended to March 10, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. in the sponsor’s stated EST zone; separate awards have other dates.
apply: Create a portal account, complete the eligibility form, then submit each matching scholarship’s separate application and required uploads. Most request a transcript, resume, financial information and FAFSA summary where applicable; written responses or videos and references depend on the fund. Some awards are administered by a school or organization.
eligibility: Primarily Central and Eastern Kentucky graduating seniors, with some undergraduate and graduate opportunities. Certain funds include Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, nationwide cystic-fibrosis students or qualifying employees’ children outside Kentucky. School, GPA, need and other restrictions vary.
notes: The main page gives the extended March 10, 2026 date, while the FAQ retains March 6, 2026. Use the main-page extension for that older cycle. Most funds combine merit and need; some are strictly merit-based. Awards may be one-time or renewable and payments go to the school.

name: BRAF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; from one-time $500 awards to four-year scholarships up to $20,000.
deadline: Dates differ by scholarship. The directory lists some recurring month/day dates and March 31, 2026 for one fund, without a full 2027 cycle. Existing award renewals have annual fall and spring document windows.
apply: Browse the directory and complete your own application through the portal, including every required document by the fund deadline. Some funds require FAFSA first. Recipients provide official verification of current full-time enrollment; renewal documents follow the specific fund’s instructions.
eligibility: Primarily Louisiana-connected students, with some funds allowing particular Louisiana or Texas colleges or University of Missouri business students. School, nomination, family or employer connection, field, GPA, need and enrollment requirements vary by fund.
notes: The main page gives a broad $500 one-time to $20,000 four-year range. Directory examples include one-time and multi-semester awards with different GPA and employment conditions. Official enrollment evidence is required; class schedules, invoices and transcripts alone are not accepted. Checks are mailed to the recipient, payable jointly to the student and school, for deposit at the school. Renewal windows are listed annually as August 1–October 31 and January 1–March 31, without cycle years.

name: Universal Scholarship Application
value: Individual scholarship amounts, duration and renewal vary; the linked older FAQ states a $500 minimum, with 2027 amounts unconfirmed.
deadline: 2027 universal application deadline is not yet posted. Some individual fund pages say to check back in January 2027; the 2026 universal application closed March 9, 2026.
apply: Complete the universal application for participating funds, then any requested follow-up questions. Search the directory for separate applications and deadlines. Common materials include an essay, transcript and academic reference; the older linked FAQ also lists a resume, financial-aid report and work or volunteer reference where requested.
eligibility: Mostly central Ohio students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: The 2026 general deadline was extended from March 1 to March 9, 2026; other fund deadlines were unchanged. The linked two-page FAQ is older and does not confirm 2027 documents. Recipients follow award-letter instructions for enrollment proof, renewal criteria and institutional payment.

name: SVCF-managed scholarships
value: Individual award amounts, duration and renewal vary by scholarship.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted; the 2026-27 cycle is closed.
apply: Use the SVCF-managed application and complete each matching fund’s additional requirements. The FAQ requires one non-family recommendation of up to 800 words, submitted by the recommender, plus applicable transcripts and financial-aid documentation. All materials are due by the application deadline; confirm the 2027 update.
eligibility: Primarily California or Bay Area-connected students, including high school seniors, undergraduates, graduate/professional students, re-entry students and vocational/technical candidates. Some funds accept noncitizens, including AB 540, DACA and legal residents. School, field, GPA, financial need, residence and enrollment requirements differ.
notes: Close to 700 awards and more than $4.5 million describe aggregate annual funding, not individual awards. The 2026-27 SVCF-managed application is closed. Students may receive only one SVCF scholarship per year, and recipients eligible for renewal or deferment may not apply for a new scholarship that year. Payments require admission/enrollment verification and a Proof of Enrollment form; continuation and deferral depend on the award.

name: Universal scholarship application
value: Individual award amounts, duration and renewal vary by fund.
deadline: 2027 deadline has not been posted. The foundation says to check back in December for the next scholarship cycle. The previous universal cycle ran December 15, 2025 to February 27, 2026.
apply: Complete the universal application’s initial eligibility questions, then each matching scholarship’s additional requirements. Other funds require separate applications. Common documents are a recent unofficial transcript, non-family or non-friend references, essays, activities and financial information. FAFSA is not required to apply.
eligibility: Primarily Colorado-connected high school seniors, undergraduates, graduate students, trade/vocational students and nontraditional learners, with different school, residence, field, merit, financial need and background requirements by fund.
notes: The $12 million figure is total 2025 funding across 84 scholarship funds, not an individual award. The latest universal cycle ran December 15, 2025–February 27, 2026; the FAQ says check back in December, without confirmed 2027 dates. Recipients complete a follow-up form before institutional payment, and renewal or summer use depends on the award. The Denver Foundation is a different organization from Denver Scholarship Foundation.

name: GRCF general scholarship application
value: Most individual awards range from $2,000 to $5,000 for the upcoming school year; amounts and future renewal vary by fund.
deadline: General applications open December 1 and close March 1 at 11:59 p.m. annually. The pages do not specify a 2027 cycle year or closing time zone. Separate funds have their own applications.
apply: Complete the general application through GoApply using your education history and recent transcript or grade report, financial information and actual or estimated Student Aid Index, and personal statements. The current FAQ lists four statements of no more than 3,000 characters each; check the new cycle’s form. The foundation matches funds automatically.
eligibility: Students with current or past West Michigan connections pursuing college, graduate school or career training, with specific county, school, field, GPA and other donor restrictions. Financial need is generally important; household income above $100,000 is described as less likely to receive an award, not an eligibility cutoff.
notes: FAFSA-ineligible applicants may use the Federal Student Aid Estimator. Scholarships are paid to the institution after acceptance for the upcoming school year; up to $500 may cover costs not billed directly by the college. The FAQ’s four 3,000-character statements differ from an older 500-word goals-statement tip on the same page. Individual continuation rules are not stated in the general guide.
